messages:
alex: Heads up — support just escalated multiple customers in EU-WEST reporting p99 spikes on /v1/generate since ~09:25 UTC. Affected model: redwood-v1-medium-quant. CPU on pods looks fine but tail latency jumps to ~2.8s (baseline ~300ms).
rita: Saw the ticket, digging into traces now. Are these requests heavy token counts? any recent deploys?
alex: Support says typical payloads (prompt ~80 tokens, max_tokens=256). No deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot.
samir: Pulling traces from observability. p95 is ok, p99 and p999 are spiking for a subset of domains. Looks correlated with a single cluster shard in eu-west-1b.
jordan: Adding initial mitigation suggestions: 1) enable temporary route-level rate limit to protect runtime, 2) enable circuit breaker to reject requests over 3s, 3) fallback to redwood-v1-small for non-critical customers.
alex: Support-bot posted customer repro snippet: ``curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-medium-quant","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":256}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq .``
samir: Trace sample (abbreviated): ``serve_latency_ms: 2824, kernel_wait_ms: 1700, kv_cache_miss: true, batching_wait_ms: 900`` — looks like a batching corner causing long queueing for some requests.
rita: If batching wait is high, we should lower max_batch_wait or enable dynamic batching thresholds for this shard. I'll increase the per-shard batching cutoff to 120ms to reduce tail queueing.
jordan: Also recommend temp routing policy to fall back to 'fast-path' model variant. Quick config (applied as emergency override):
```
route: "/v1/generate"
conditions:
  region: "eu-west"
  priority: "emergency"
actions:
  fallback_model: "redwood-v1-small"
  max_batch_wait_ms: 120
  rate_limit: 1000rps
```
alex: Can someone apply that override and monitor p99 for the shard?
rita: Applying now to shard eu-west-1b. Patch id: emergency-3032.
oncall-bot: deploy override emergency-3032 started by rita at 09:37:12 UTC.
samir: Quick probe after override: p99 reduced from 2.8s -> 760ms within two minutes. kernel_wait still elevated but batching wait dropped.
jordan: Good. Next steps: 1) keep override for 30m, 2) run canary with reduced max_tokens=128 for 10% of traffic, 3) schedule a deeper postmortem to find kernel stalls.
alex: I'm notifying support to update customers and throttle heavy workloads. @support-bot please apply per-customer soft rate limits for the top 3 impacted accounts.
support-bot: Soft limits applied to accounts A123, B456, C789 at 09:40 UTC (rate reduced to 60% of baseline).
rita: Creating follow-up ticket: investigate kernel wait cause (likely kernel scheduling on older GPU nodes or memory pressure). tagging eng-runtime + eng-infra.
samir: For immediate SLO guardrail improvements I suggest adding this to oncall playbook: - automatic fallback to smaller model after p99 > 1.2s for 2 consecutive minutes, - circuit breaker to return 503 after 3s serve time, - route-level burst token bucket with enforcement.
jordan: I'll draft the playbook snippet and add to repo. Also recommend metric alert: p99_eu_west > 1.2s for 2m -> page oncall.
alex: Thanks team. Keeping override until 10:10 UTC unless we see regression. Please post any anomalies here. :thumbsup:
rita: noted, monitoring dashboards.
samir: logging the key traces to ticket 6742 for root-cause analysis.
jordan: small reminder: ensure fallback model produces acceptable output for affected prompt sets — we'll run quick evals against sample prompts.
alex: Closing the escalation channel in 30m if stable. Thanks all.
